title: A common signup-form email regex rejects o'brien@example.com but accepts user+tag@example.com
assumption: A regex like ^[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$ is a reasonable, slightly-strict stand-in for "is this a valid email address".

input.description: A signup, checkout, or newsletter form's email field, validated client- or server-side with a hand-written regex, used by a person whose email address's local part (the part before @) contains a punctuation character the regex author didn't anticipate - most commonly an apostrophe in a surname.

what_goes_wrong: `/^[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$/` rejects `o'brien@example.com` (valid, real-world mail address) while accepting `user+tag@example.com` (plus-addressing, also valid) - the regex's author remembered to allow `+` for Gmail-style tagging but not `'`, so a real customer's real address bounces at the form while a less common but equally valid syntax sails through.
why: RFC 5322 section 3.2.3 defines the characters allowed in an unquoted local-part (`atext`) as letters, digits and `! # $ % & ' * + - / = ? ^ _ ` { | } ~`, so the apostrophe is exactly as legal as `+` (a dot is also allowed, but only between such characters). A regex built from `\w` (letters, digits, underscore) plus a hand-picked handful of extras will inevitably miss some of that list, and the apostrophe is a costly one to miss because it appears in real surnames such as O'Brien and D'Angelo, so the regex rejects real customers rather than malformed input.
affects: any email validator built from a hand-picked character class instead of RFC 5322's atext
fix: Don't hand-roll an email-syntax regex. Validate only loosely for form UX (e.g. "contains exactly one @, with non-whitespace on both sides") and rely on the actual downstream proof that matters - whether sending a confirmation email to the address succeeds - rather than a regex meant to approximate RFC 5322's full grammar.

sources.title: RFC 5322: Internet Message Format, Section 3.2.3 (Atom / atext)
RFC 5321: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, Section 4.1.2 (Mailbox local-part)

test_cases.note: their_is_valid_email(address) should accept this RFC-5322-legal address rather than rejecting it for containing an apostrophe.
Plus-addressing is also legal atext and should be accepted.
